messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Stan in the Juliabox
parts:
Hi, Julia experts!  Can anyone set up the Juliabox:  https://www.juliabox.org
so it can do Stan models?  I don’t really know where to start here, but I guess if someone could set up a standard example such as the 8 schools so that a naive non-Julia-user (e.g., me) could be able to run it from the browser, that would be great.

If we can get this working, then we could build a Stanbox (i.e., the Juliabox with a wrapper full of Stan logos), then potential users could play with Stan in the Stanbox (sounds like Sandbox! cool!) and see it working, without having to go thru the steps of installing Stan on their computer.

!

See you
A

messages.author: 512610f4917ceaf3
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Stan in the Juliabox
parts:
Andrew,

Stan is installed and available for everyone on JuliaBox, so it is completely ready to go. To use JuliaBox you do need a JuliaBox account.

If you don’t have a JuliaBox account yet, an email to Viral (cc-ed) I believe is the easiest way to set this up. Maybe it is also possible to create a general demo account shared for Stan-related demo purposes, but I’m not sure if this is acceptable to JuliaBox.org. 

If you have a JuliaBox account, just log in using the browser. Below I have attached 2 example notebooks, including the EightSchools example. The Bernoulli example is also on Stan.jl on Github.

JuliaBox gives you your own file space to store Julia and Stan scripts. Once you log in, you can upload the 2 example files (using the ‘Files’ menu item) and open them from the 'IJulia' menu item (by clicking one of the files that you have just uploaded).

I don’t know how familiar you are with Notebook-like interfaces, so it is difficult to gauge exactly how to best help setting it up and get you going, but I’m more than happy to help out.

Regards,
Rob J. Goedman
goe...@mac.com
